first aider = a person trained to give basic medical help
blood donor = a person who gives blood to help patients
neighbourhood watch = local people who watch for crime and help the police
queue up = to stand in a line and wait your turn
break the law = to do something illegal
keep the peace = to stop fighting and keep a place calm
tell the truth = to say what really happened
tell a lie = to say something that is not true
fair = treating people equally and in the right way
justice = fair treatment according to the law
duty = something you must do because it is right or the law
civic duty = something a citizen should do for society, such as voting
public place = a place that anyone can use, such as a park or station
private property = land or a building that belongs to a person or company
no parking = a sign that you must not leave a car there
speed camera = a camera that photographs cars going too fast
seat belt law = the rule that you must wear a seat belt in a car
age limit = the youngest or oldest age allowed for something
ID check = when someone asks to see proof of your age or identity
curfew = a time after which you must stay inside
